An honest 2026 comparison of Artisan and 11x across the sales journey, from finding prospects to booking meetings, with real strengths on both sides. Jaspar Carmichael-Jack 9 minutes read · Jul 20, 2026 Key Takeaways Artisan runs the full BDR (business development representative) job in one platform: sourcing from over 270M B2B contacts, enrichment, multichannel outreach, reply handling, and meeting booking, with Ava as autonomous as you set her to be. Over 90% of Artisan customers run Ava autonomously. 11x offers Alice for multichannel outreach and Julian, an AI phone agent, and has raised roughly $74M from investors including a16z and Benchmark. 11x sells through enterprise-style contracts (reported pricing around $5,000/month, long onboarding, no self-serve) while sitting in the lower mid-market by capability. Artisan charges for work performed, not seats, with a free trial. 11x drew attributed scrutiny in 2025: TechCrunch reported customer claims the company could not support (March 24, 2025), and its founder-CEO stepped down to non-executive chairman on May 5, 2025. Artisan's dialer runs inside the same sequences at $67/seat/month with unlimited minutes, roughly a third of what dedicated parallel dialers charge. Artisan is SOC 2 Type II compliant, with SSO, SAML, and role-based access on Enterprise plans. Artisan and 11x both sell an AI sales rep that runs outbound for you, but they solve the job differently. Artisan is the better fit for most teams: one platform where Ava owns prospecting through booked meeting, with usage-based pricing and no seat fees. 11x offers multichannel outreach plus an AI phone agent and can suit a specific buyer. Neither tool is a set of features you assemble. Both promise an AI employee who works the pipeline while your reps sell. The real question is which one does more of that job reliably, and at what commercial cost. This comparison walks the sales journey stage by stage, credits what 11x actually does well, and ends with honest scenarios for picking either one.
